name: Garni Temple
description: A reconstructed Ionic temple stands on a basalt cliff above the Azat gorge in Garni. Walk the platform for columns against the canyon and the surrounding fortress walls.

name: Geghard Monastery
description: Geghard’s churches and rock-cut chambers sit in a mountain gorge east of Yerevan. Some chapels are carved straight into the cliff, with light falling through openings in the stone.

name: Etchmiadzin Cathedral
description: The Mother See cathedral in Vagharshapat is the spiritual centre of the Armenian Apostolic Church. The complex of churches and museums surrounds a courtyard open to visitors.
photo_credit: Author of the photo is Heretiq · Public domain

name: Amberd Fortress
description: Amberd’s stone walls crown a ridge on the slopes of Mount Aragats. A medieval church stands inside the fortress ruins with wide views over the highland valleys.

name: Zvartnots Cathedral
description: The ruined circular cathedral of Zvartnots sits in an open archaeological park west of Yerevan. Walk among the column bases and carved stones with Ararat on the horizon on clear days.

name: Mount Ararat
description: From Khor Virap monastery on Armenia’s Ararat plain, Mount Ararat fills the southern sky. The stamp uses this Armenian viewpoint; the summit itself lies across the border in Türkiye.

name: Cascade
description: Yerevan’s Cascade climbs in limestone terraces from Tamanyan sculpture park toward the Monument district. Escalators inside help you rise between outdoor art platforms and city views.

name: Republic Square
description: Republic Square is Yerevan’s main oval plaza of pink tufa government buildings and museums. In the evening the fountains and facades light up for a slow walk around the oval.

name: Vernissage
description: Vernissage is Yerevan’s open-air market for crafts, art, and souvenirs along Khanjyan and nearby streets. Weekend stalls are the busiest for handmade pieces and Soviet-era finds.

name: GUM Market
description: GUM Market on Khorenatsi is a covered hall of spice, produce, and prepared-food counters. Wander the aisles for dried fruit, cheese, and a quick taste of Yerevan’s market culture.

name: Dolmama
description: Dolmama is a long-running restaurant on Pushkin Street known for refined takes on Armenian home cooking. The stamp marks the venue location — check current hours before you go.

name: Pandok Yerevan
description: Pandok Yerevan (Tavern Yerevan) on Zakyan Street serves hearty Armenian tavern fare in the city centre. Come for grilled meats and shared plates in a casual setting.

name: Sherep
description: Sherep sits near Republic Square and focuses on contemporary Armenian cooking. The stamp uses the mapped restaurant point on Pap Tagavor Street.
photo_credit: Shaun Dunphy from Lindfield, United Kingdom · CC BY-SA 2.0

name: Lavash
description: Lavash restaurant on Tumanyan Street is named for Armenia’s flatbread and serves modern Armenian dishes. Confirm opening times on the day you visit.
photo_credit: Shaun Dunphy from Lindfield, United Kingdom · CC BY-SA 2.0

name: In Vino
description: In Vino on Saryan Street is a well-known wine bar in Yerevan’s wine-bar strip. Taste Armenian bottles by the glass in a compact, walk-in space.

name: The Club
description: The Club (Akumb) on Tumanyan Street mixes dining with a cultural-club atmosphere in central Yerevan. Use the mapped point; programmes and hours can change.

name: Pak Shuka
description: Pak Shuka (the Covered Market) on Mashtots Avenue is a classic Yerevan food market for produce and pantry goods. Browse the counters for fruit, herbs, and picnic supplies.

name: Caucasus Pandok
description: Caucasus Pandok on Hanrapetutyan Street serves Caucasian and Armenian tavern dishes in central Yerevan. A straightforward stop for shared plates and grilled food.

name: Dargett Craft Beer
description: Dargett is a Yerevan craft brewery taproom on Aram Street. Stop in for house beers on tap; the stamp marks the brewpub node, not a beer brand partnership.

name: Yerevan Wine Days
description: Yerevan Wine Days turns Saryan, Tumanyan, and Moskovyan streets into an open-air wine festival, usually on the first weekend of June. It is seasonal and limited to those festival days — check yerewinedays.am for the current dates.

name: Sevanavank
description: A monastic peninsula on Lake Sevan with twin churches above the water.
